scope: Every real convex h on Ici T tending to infinity, every natural j>=1, every real M; actual windows wholly above max T M, affine rise at least j, and defect between 0 and 1 throughout the closed window.
findings: Actual inverse unit levels are obtained using convex continuity and the intermediate value theorem. Strict increase, divergence, and decreasing increments are proved.
Non-summability follows by telescoping the actual increments; eventual geometric decay contradicts it via residue-class summability.
Supporting slopes are constructed as a real supremum, and convexity bounds the endpoint defects on the full window.
No differentiability, inverse-level sequence, near-affine-window premise, project axiom, or additional result claim is introduced.
citation_note: The recorded source cites the inverse-increment idea as Lemma 2.7; the accessible author PDF has Lemma 2.6. Preserve the recorded citation qualification until arXiv v3 numbering is directly checked.
